courses.centralQuestion: What exactly does the API promise, and how can providers and consumers verify that promise?
courses.incomingBoundary: Basic programming ability and no assumed OpenAPI experience.
courses.outgoingBoundary: A frozen API 1.1 contract, operation ledger, schema fixtures, security decisions, workflows, and provider-neutral behavioral scenarios.
courses.responsibility: Define and verify the public HTTP contract.
courses.title: OpenAPI Contract Engineering

courses.centralQuestion: Which internal mechanisms keep the public contract true under concurrency, restart, and partial failure?
courses.incomingBoundary: The immutable Course 1 API 1.1 handoff and its provider-neutral proof corpus.
courses.outgoingBoundary: A durable API 1.2 service handoff with migrations 001–005, idempotency, optimistic concurrency, stable pagination, worker recovery, artifact integrity, and transactional webhook delivery.
courses.responsibility: Implement the fixed contract with durable application, database, worker, storage, and release mechanisms.
courses.title: Contract-Driven API Service Engineering

courses.centralQuestion: How does the service remain trustworthy under hostile behavior without hiding behind middleware or scanner output?
courses.incomingBoundary: The Course 2 API 1.2 durable-service handoff and migrations 001–005.
courses.outgoingBoundary: Security Profile 1.0, migrations 006–007, threat-to-requirement traceability, identity and authorization policy, hostile-input vectors, secure webhook rules, abuse controls, and incident evidence.
courses.responsibility: Preserve the API and durable-service guarantees when callers, credentials, inputs, destinations, and dependencies are not trusted by default.
courses.title: API Security Engineering

courses.centralQuestion: How do operators know whether the user promise is still true, and how do they recover it without making the incident worse?
courses.incomingBoundary: The Course 3 API 1.2 service protected by Security Profile 1.0 and migrations 001–007.
courses.outgoingBoundary: Reliability Profile 1.0, migration 008, critical journeys, deadlines, resilience policies, lifecycle controls, telemetry contracts, SLOs, alerts, runbooks, game-day evidence, and reconciliation plans.
courses.responsibility: Detect, diagnose, contain, reconcile, and recover when processes, dependencies, networks, or operators fail.
courses.title: API Reliability and Observability Engineering

courses.centralQuestion: Where does time and capacity go, what is the first limiting resource, and which measured change improves the system without weakening its promise?
courses.incomingBoundary: The Course 4 observable and recoverable API 1.2 service with Security and Reliability Profiles 1.0 and migrations 001–008.
courses.outgoingBoundary: Performance Profile 1.0, migration 009, workload identities, benchmark evidence, HTTP and query optimizations, concurrency and cache policy, traffic controls, capacity models, and performance release gates.
courses.responsibility: Preserve correctness, latency, throughput, fairness, and bounded resource use as demand and data volume grow.
courses.title: API Performance, Capacity, and Traffic Engineering

courses.centralQuestion: How can independent producers and consumers share durable facts without confusing intent, delivery attempts, processing effects, and historical truth?
courses.incomingBoundary: The Course 5 API 1.2 service with Security, Reliability, and Performance Profiles 1.0 and migrations 001–009.
courses.outgoingBoundary: Analysis Events API 1.0, Event Profile 1.0, AsyncAPI 3.1.0 contract, CloudEvents 1.0 envelope profile, migrations 010–012, replay and dead-letter policy, and governed consumer declarations.
courses.responsibility: Design, evolve, secure, operate, and verify asynchronous contracts when delivery may be delayed, duplicated, reordered within declared limits, or replayed.
courses.title: Event-Driven API Engineering
